Guiding vector fields for the distributed motion coordination of mobile robots, explained

The paper (Yao, García de Marina, Sun, Cao), written out step by step for 21 robots on three concentric paths: from one robot and its virtual coordinate, to a team that keeps its spacing, to surfaces, collisions and fixed-wing aircraft, down to the program each robot runs

Published

November 15, 2026

From the Swarm Systems Lab, University of Granada. To try the results by hand, open the playground.

What this page does. It takes the paper Guiding vector fields for the distributed motion coordination of mobile robots (its LaTeX source, multi_jrn_main.tex) and writes it out for one of the paper’s own examples: 21 robots on three concentric paths, seven on each, that keep equal spacings in their path parameters (the paper’s third simulation). It goes step by step: one robot and its virtual coordinate (Section II-C of the paper), the coordination component that couples the robots (Section III), why it works from any start (Theorem 1), surfaces instead of paths (Section IV, Theorem 2), collisions (Section V), and fixed-wing aircraft at constant speed (Section VI, Theorem 3). It ends with the program each robot runs, and with the paper’s four simulations and two flights run again.

Source and status. The results are the paper’s, and this page does not re-prove them. It adds a few things of its own, each marked where it appears: one reading of the Lyapunov derivative (Section 4.2), the speed of the coordination on a path (Section 4.4), and two remarks on the proofs (Section 4.3). Every number on the page is computed by core.py when the page is rendered. The interactive figures run assets/core.js, and make check proves that the two agree.

1 The problem

NN robots move in ℝn\mathbb R^n (n=2n = 2 in the example, n=3n = 3 for the aircraft). Robot ii is a single integrator, ẋ[i]=u[i]\dot x^{[i]} = u^{[i]}, until Section 7 replaces it with a fixed-wing aircraft.

Its path. Robot ii has its own path, given by a parametrisation x=f[i](w)x = f^{[i]}(w), w∈ℝw \in \mathbb R. Different robots may have different paths. A path may cross itself, need not be closed, and need not be given by an implicit equation. Only f[i]f^{[i]} and its first two derivatives are needed, and they must be bounded (Assumption 2).

What it measures. Its own position x[i]x^{[i]} (a GPS on the aircraft of the paper). Nothing about the other robots’ positions, except in Section 6, where it measures the positions of the robots close to it.

What is shared. Each robot keeps one number of its own, the virtual coordinate w[i]w^{[i]}: where it is on its path, in the units of the parameter. It sends that number to its neighbours in an undirected graph, and receives theirs (Remark 2). For every neighbour jj it knows a desired difference Δ[i,j]=−Δ[j,i]\Delta^{[i,j]} = -\Delta^{[j,i]}.

The task (Problem 1). From any start, every robot converges to its path, ∥Φ[i]∥→0\|\Phi^{[i]}\| \to 0, and every edge reaches its desired difference, w[i]−w[j]−Δ[i,j]→0w^{[i]} - w^{[j]} - \Delta^{[i,j]} \to 0.

Why it is hard. Nothing tells the robots where to be at what time: there is no clock to follow, no leader, and no common frame on the path. Each robot only knows its own path and a few numbers from its neighbours, and the team must agree on its spacing while it moves. The paper does this with one extra coordinate per robot, and the field it builds has no point where it vanishes, so no start is a trap.

The example. The paper’s third simulation (its Fig. 5). Robots 1 to 7 are on the circle of radius a=10a = 10, robots 8 to 14 on the ellipse with half-axes a=10a = 10 and b=5b = 5, and robots 15 to 21 on the circle of radius b=5b = 5:

f[i](w)=(10cos⁡w10sin⁡w),f[i](w)=(10cos⁡w5sin⁡w),f[i](w)=(5cos⁡w5sin⁡w). f^{[i]}(w) = \begin{pmatrix} 10\cos w \\ 10 \sin w \end{pmatrix},\qquad f^{[i]}(w) = \begin{pmatrix} 10\cos w \\ 5 \sin w \end{pmatrix},\qquad f^{[i]}(w) = \begin{pmatrix} 5\cos w \\ 5 \sin w \end{pmatrix}.

The graph is the cycle 1−2−…−21−11 - 2 - \dots - 21 - 1: each robot talks to two others. The spacing is equal in the path parameter: the reference is w[i]*=(i−1)2π/21w^{[i]*} = (i-1)\,2\pi/21, so Δ[i,i+1]=−2π/21\Delta^{[i,i+1]} = -2\pi/21 for the first 20 edges and Δ[21,1]=20⋅2π/21\Delta^{[21,1]} = 20 \cdot 2\pi/21 for the edge that closes the cycle. The gains are k1=k2=1k_1 = k_2 = 1 and kc=100k_c = 100.

2 Step 1: one robot and its virtual coordinate

2.1 A path one dimension up

A path in ℝn\mathbb R^n is the zero set of nn functions once ww is a coordinate of its own (Section II-C of the paper). With the generalised coordinate ξ=(x1,…,xn,w)∈ℝn+1\xi = (x_1, \dots, x_n, w) \in \mathbb R^{n+1} and

ϕj(ξ)=xj−fj(w),j=1,…,n, \phi_j(\xi) = x_j - f_j(w), \qquad j = 1, \dots, n,

the set where all the ϕj\phi_j vanish is the graph of the path, {(f(w),w)}\{(f(w), w)\}, a curve in ℝn+1\mathbb R^{n+1} that never crosses itself, even when ff does: two points of it with the same xx have different ww. The paper’s field (1) is a wedge product of the gradients ∇ϕj\nabla\phi_j, which runs along that curve, minus a term that pulls towards it:

χ(ξ)=∧(∇ϕ1,…,∇ϕn)−∑j=1nkjϕj∇ϕj. \chi(\xi) = \wedge\left(\nabla\phi_1, \dots, \nabla\phi_n\right) - \sum_{j=1}^n k_j\,\phi_j\,\nabla\phi_j .

Written out, it is (3):

χ=((−1)nf1′(w)−k1ϕ1⋮(−1)nfn′(w)−knϕn(−1)n+∑lklϕlfl′(w)). \chi = \begin{pmatrix} (-1)^n f_1'(w) - k_1\phi_1 \\ \vdots \\ (-1)^n f_n'(w) - k_n\phi_n \\ (-1)^n + \sum_{l} k_l\,\phi_l\, f_l'(w) \end{pmatrix}.

The first nn entries move the robot, and the last one moves ww. It never vanishes (this line is ours): if the first nn entries are zero, then kjϕj=(−1)nfj′k_j\phi_j = (-1)^n f'_j, and the last entry is (−1)n(1+∥f′∥2)≠0(-1)^n\left(1 + \|f'\|^2\right) \neq 0. This is the property of the singularity-free field that the paper builds on (its references [yao2021singularity], [yao2020mobile]).

2.2 The field for the example

For robot 8, on the ellipse (n=2n = 2, so (−1)n=1(-1)^n = 1), with k1=k2=1k_1 = k_2 = 1:

χ[8]=(−10sin⁡w−ϕ15cos⁡w−ϕ21−10ϕ1sin⁡w+5ϕ2cos⁡w),ϕ1=x1−10cos⁡w,ϕ2=x2−5sin⁡w. \chi^{[8]} = \begin{pmatrix} -10\sin w - \phi_1 \\ 5\cos w - \phi_2 \\ 1 - 10\,\phi_1 \sin w + 5\,\phi_2 \cos w \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \phi_1 = x_1 - 10\cos w,\quad \phi_2 = x_2 - 5\sin w .

On the path (ϕ=0\phi = 0) the robot moves at f′(w)f'(w) and its virtual coordinate at ẇ=1\dot w = 1: the ellipse is run counterclockwise. Off the path, ww is in a closed loop with the robot: it moves ahead faster when the robot is ahead of its guiding point f(w)f(w), and slows down or goes back when the robot is behind (the paper’s remark on the “carrot”). The figure shows a robot alone, with its guiding point.

3 Step 2: a coordination component

3.1 The coordination function

On the path, every robot’s virtual coordinate runs at the same rate, ẇ=(−1)n\dot w = (-1)^n. So differences of ww are conserved, and they are the natural thing to coordinate. The paper adds one term to the last entry of the field, (4) and (5),

χ[i]=χpf[i]+kc(0⋮0c[i]),c[i]=−∑j∈𝒩i(w[i]−w[j]−Δ[i,j]), \chi^{[i]} = \chi^{[i]}_{\mathrm{pf}} + k_c \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ c^{[i]} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad c^{[i]} = -\sum_{j \in \mathcal N_i} \left( w^{[i]} - w^{[j]} - \Delta^{[i,j]} \right),

the consensus law (7). In stacked form c=−L(w−w*)c = -L(w - w^*), with LL the Laplacian of the graph and w*w^* any reference with Δ[i,j]=w[i]*−w[j]*\Delta^{[i,j]} = w^{[i]*} - w^{[j]*} (8). The robots never need w*w^* itself, only the differences with their neighbours.

The coordination term acts only on ww. It does not push the robot: it moves the robot’s guiding point along the path, forward when the robot is behind its neighbours in ww, back when it is ahead, and the path-following part then brings the robot to its guiding point.

3.2 For the example

Robot 8 is between robot 7 (on the large circle) and robot 9 (on the ellipse):

c[8]=−(w[8]−w[7]−2π21)−(w[8]−w[9]+2π21),ẇ[8]=1−10ϕ1sin⁡w[8]+5ϕ2cos⁡w[8]+100c[8]. c^{[8]} = -\left(w^{[8]} - w^{[7]} - \tfrac{2\pi}{21}\right) - \left(w^{[8]} - w^{[9]} + \tfrac{2\pi}{21}\right), \qquad \dot w^{[8]} = 1 - 10\,\phi_1 \sin w^{[8]} + 5\,\phi_2 \cos w^{[8]} + 100\, c^{[8]} .

It sends one number, w[8]w^{[8]}, to robots 7 and 9, and receives theirs. In steady motion the team keeps w[i+1]=w[i]+2π/21w^{[i+1]} = w^{[i]} + 2\pi/21. Robots on different paths then sit at the same angle parameter but at different places, so the team makes a pattern that changes shape as it turns: the three groups bunch and spread out as they pass the axes of the ellipse (the paper’s “varying formation shapes”).

4 Step 3: why it works, from any start (Theorem 1)

4.1 The composite error

Theorem 1 of the paper: under Assumptions 1 (the graph is undirected and connected) and 2 (bounded f′f' and f″f''), with constant Δ\Delta, the field (5) with (7) solves Problem 1 globally: the composite error

e=(ΦD⊤w̃),w̃=w−w*, e = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi \\ D^\top \tilde w \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \tilde w = w - w^*,

goes to zero from any start. Φ\Phi stacks the path-following errors of all robots, and D⊤w̃D^\top\tilde w the coordination errors of all edges (DD is an incidence matrix, L=DD⊤L = DD^\top). The proof (Appendix A) uses

V=12(Φ⊤KΦ+kcw̃⊤Lw̃)=12∑iΦ[i]⊤K[i]Φ[i]+kc2∑(i,j)∈ℰ(w[i]−w[j]−Δ[i,j])2 V = \tfrac12\left(\Phi^\top K \Phi + k_c\,\tilde w^\top L\,\tilde w\right) = \tfrac12\sum_i \Phi^{[i]\top} K^{[i]} \Phi^{[i]} + \tfrac{k_c}{2}\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal E}\left(w^{[i]} - w^{[j]} - \Delta^{[i,j]}\right)^2

(41), and finds (45)

V̇=−∥KΦ∥2−∥𝔉⊤KΦ−kcLw̃∥2≤0, \dot V = -\|K\Phi\|^2 - \left\|\mathfrak F^\top K\Phi - k_c L\tilde w\right\|^2 \le 0,

with 𝔉=diag⁡(f[1]′,…,f[N]′)\mathfrak F = \operatorname{diag}(f^{[1]\prime}, \dots, f^{[N]\prime}).

4.2 What V̇\dot V says

The ii-th entry of 𝔉⊤KΦ−kcLw̃\mathfrak F^\top K\Phi - k_c L\tilde w is f[i]′⊤K[i]Φ[i]+kcc[i]f^{[i]\prime\top}K^{[i]}\Phi^{[i]} + k_c c^{[i]}, and by (38) that is ẇ[i]−(−1)n\dot w^{[i]} - (-1)^n. So (this reading is ours)

V̇=−∥KΦ∥2−∑i(ẇ[i]−(−1)n)2. \dot V = -\|K\Phi\|^2 - \sum_i \left(\dot w^{[i]} - (-1)^n\right)^2 .

VV falls as long as some robot is off its path, or some robot’s virtual coordinate runs at another rate than the nominal one. A team whose robots are on their paths and whose ww’s all run at the nominal rate has V̇=0\dot V = 0, and then, since every ẇ[i]\dot w^{[i]} equals (−1)n(-1)^n and c[i]=0c^{[i]} = 0 for all ii, every edge is at its desired difference. This is how core.py computes V̇\dot V. Against a finite difference of VV along the example’s run, the largest relative gap is 1.3e-05:

time VV V̇\dot V from (45) V̇\dot V, finite difference
0.0 s 7587 -3.20226e+06 -3.20222e+06
0.5 s 432.8 -667.411 -667.411
5.0 s 9.286 -5.28515 -5.28515

4.3 Two remarks on the proofs

Both are ours, and neither changes a result.

  • Theorem 1 cites LaSalle’s invariance principle (Khalil, Theorem 4.4). That theorem asks for an autonomous system with a compact positively invariant set. The state is ξ\xi, which contains every w[i]w^{[i]}, and the ww’s grow without bound (they run at (−1)n(-1)^n), so no sublevel set of VV is compact in ξ\xi. The error dynamics (40) do not close in ee either: they depend on ww through 𝔉\mathfrak F. The proof of Theorem 2 (Appendix B) uses Barbalat’s lemma instead, with Assumption 3, and that argument covers the path case as it stands (one parameter instead of two). So Theorem 1 holds; its proof is the one of Theorem 2.
  • Connectivity (Assumption 1) is not what makes the edges converge. The proof shows D⊤w̃→0D^\top\tilde w \to 0, which is the coordination error of every edge, for any graph. What connectivity adds is that the edges then fix every pair of robots. On a graph cut in two, each part coordinates, and the offset between the parts is whatever the transient left. The figure above has the cut; the playground’s census runs it on random teams.

4.4 How fast

Theorem 1 says nothing about how fast. A short linearisation shows what sets the speed (ours, checked against the simulation). Take robots on a circle of radius aa, with K=kIK = kI, and write each Φ\Phi in the frame of the path: Φt\Phi_t along it, Φn\Phi_n across it. The frame turns with ww, which couples the two. For one mode of the Laplacian, with eigenvalue λ\lambda, near the path:

ddt(ΦtΦnw̃)=(−k(1+a2)−1kcaλ1−k0ka0−kcλ)(ΦtΦnw̃). \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\begin{pmatrix} \Phi_t \\ \Phi_n \\ \tilde w \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -k(1+a^2) & -1 & k_c\, a\, \lambda \\ 1 & -k & 0 \\ k\,a & 0 & -k_c\lambda \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \Phi_t \\ \Phi_n \\ \tilde w \end{pmatrix}.

Its slowest eigenvalue sets the rate of the coordination. The table compares it with the rate measured on three robots on the circle (λ=3\lambda = 3), one of them pushed ahead by 0.20.2 in ww:

radius aa kck_c kk slowest rate, linearisation rate measured, simulation
2 1 1 0.746 0.606
5 1 1 0.229 0.229
10 0.5 1 0.029 0.029
5 1 3 0.124 0.124
5 20 1 0.853 0.867

When kcλk_c\lambda is small next to k(1+a2)k(1+a^2), the slowest rate is close to kcλ(1+k2)/(k2(1+a2))k_c\lambda\,(1+k^2)\,/\,\left(k^2(1+a^2)\right): the coordination slows down as 1/∥f′∥21/\|f'\|^2. The robot must travel ∥f′∥\|f'\| in space for every unit of ww it corrects, and the path-following term, which grows as ∥f′∥2\|f'\|^2, holds it to its guiding point. This explains a choice in the paper. On the figure eight of its first simulation ∥f′∥\|f'\| goes up to 36.7, and the slowest mode of the cycle of 50 robots has λ2\lambda_2 = 0.016. With the mean of ∥f′∥2\|f'\|^2 along the eight in the estimate above, the time constant of that mode would be about 5.8 hours with kc=1k_c = 1. The paper takes kc=300k_c = 300, “large to accelerate the motion coordination”, and the estimate drops to about 69.1 s, which is the scale of its Fig. 3 [numerical].

5 Step 4: surfaces (Theorem 2)

5.1 Two virtual coordinates and an extra vector

A surface needs two parameters, x=f[i](w1,w2)x = f^{[i]}(w_1, w_2), and each robot keeps two virtual coordinates. The generalised coordinate is ξ=(x,w1,w2)∈ℝn+2\xi = (x, w_1, w_2) \in \mathbb R^{n+2}, and the nn gradients ∇ϕj\nabla\phi_j are not enough for a wedge product in n+2n + 2 dimensions. The paper adds an extra vector vv (14), and with v=(0,…,0,vn+1,vn+2)v = (0, \dots, 0, v_{n+1}, v_{n+2}) the field is (15):

χsf=(−1)n(vn+2∂w1f−vn+1∂w2fvn+2−vn+1)+(−KΦ∂w1f⊤KΦ∂w2f⊤KΦ). \chi_{\mathrm{sf}} = (-1)^n \begin{pmatrix} v_{n+2}\,\partial_{w_1} f - v_{n+1}\,\partial_{w_2} f \\ v_{n+2} \\ -v_{n+1} \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} -K\Phi \\ \partial_{w_1} f^\top K\Phi \\ \partial_{w_2} f^\top K\Phi \end{pmatrix}.

On a surface a robot has a direction to choose, and vv chooses it. Theorem 2 takes v=(−1)n+1(0,…,0,ẇ2*,−ẇ1*)v = (-1)^{n+1}(0, \dots, 0, \dot w_2^*, -\dot w_1^*). With that choice the field reads (this rewriting is ours)

χsf=(∂w1fẇ1*+∂w2fẇ2*−KΦẇ1*+∂w1f⊤KΦẇ2*+∂w2f⊤KΦ), \chi_{\mathrm{sf}} = \begin{pmatrix} \partial_{w_1} f\,\dot w_1^* + \partial_{w_2} f\,\dot w_2^* - K\Phi \\ \dot w_1^* + \partial_{w_1} f^\top K\Phi \\ \dot w_2^* + \partial_{w_2} f^\top K\Phi \end{pmatrix},

which is the path field of Step 1 with (−1)n(-1)^n replaced by the desired parametric speeds ẇ*\dot w^*: on the surface the robot moves at ∂w1fẇ1*+∂w2fẇ2*\partial_{w_1} f\,\dot w_1^* + \partial_{w_2} f\,\dot w_2^*, and its virtual coordinates at ẇ*\dot w^*. Each parameter gets its own consensus term (16), (19), with gains kc1,kc2k_{c1}, k_{c2}, and each robot sends two numbers.

Theorem 2: under Assumptions 1 and 3 (bounded first and second derivatives), with constant Δ1\Delta_1, Δ2\Delta_2, the field solves Problem 2 globally: every robot converges to its surface, every edge to its two desired differences, and every robot’s virtual coordinates to the speeds ẇ*\dot w^*. The Lyapunov function is (55), the same as above with one consensus term per parameter, and the reading of Section 4.2 carries over: V̇=−∥KΦ∥2−∑i,p(ẇp[i]−ẇp*)2\dot V = -\|K\Phi\|^2 - \sum_{i,p}\left(\dot w_p^{[i]} - \dot w^*_p\right)^2.

5.2 The sphere of Example 2

The paper’s Example 2 puts two robots on the unit sphere (12),

f=(cos⁡w1cos⁡w2,cos⁡w1sin⁡w2,sin⁡w1), f = (\cos w_1 \cos w_2,\ \cos w_1\sin w_2,\ \sin w_1),

with Δ1[1,2]=Δ2[1,2]=−π\Delta^{[1,2]}_1 = \Delta^{[1,2]}_2 = -\pi, in two scenarios: ẇ*=(0,1)\dot w^* = (0, 1) and ẇ*=(1,1)\dot w^* = (1, 1) (its Fig. 1). Here n=3n = 3, so v=(0,0,0,ẇ2*,−ẇ1*)v = (0, 0, 0, \dot w_2^*, -\dot w_1^*). Shifting both parameters by π\pi keeps cos⁡w1cos⁡w2\cos w_1 \cos w_2 and cos⁡w1sin⁡w2\cos w_1 \sin w_2 and changes the sign of sin⁡w1\sin w_1: robot 2 sits at robot 1’s mirror image across the equator. In the first scenario both run along parallels, one north and one south; in the second their paths wind over the sphere. After 20 s of the run below, the largest path error is 4.7e-04 and the coordination error 1.5e-07.

6 Step 5: collisions (Section V)

The coordination is in parameter space. Two robots with different ww can still be at the same place: on a path that crosses itself, or on two paths that cross. The paper’s first simulation spreads its 50 robots over half of the figure eight, w[i]*=(i−1)T/(2N)w^{[i]*} = (i-1)\,T/(2N), and this is why: the eight crosses itself at w=0w = 0 and w=πw = \pi, so two robots half a period apart reach the crossing at the same time. Spread eight robots over the whole period and they meet there twice a lap: the closest two come within 0.006 of each other. Over half the period they never come closer than 4.98.

Section V of the paper adds a safety barrier certificate (Wang, Ames, Egerstedt 2017). With a safety distance RR, hij=∥P(ξ[i]−ξ[j])∥2−R2h_{ij} = \|P(\xi^{[i]} - \xi^{[j]})\|^2 - R^2 (where PP keeps the position and drops ww) and Bij=1/hijB_{ij} = 1/h_{ij} (23), each robot solves its own small quadratic program (QP2): the command closest to its field χ[i]\chi^{[i]} with

(ξ[j]−ξ[i])⊤P⊤χ̌[i]≤α4hij3for j∈𝒟i. (\xi^{[j]} - \xi^{[i]})^\top P^\top \check\chi^{[i]} \le \tfrac{\alpha}{4}\, h_{ij}^3 \qquad \text{for } j \in \mathcal D_i .

The constraint only touches the position part, so ww runs as before, and only robot ii’s own command is changed. It needs the positions of the robots near it, measured, not communicated. Here the page solves (QP2) with Hildreth’s method, 40 sweeps per tick.

The set 𝒟i\mathcal D_i holds the robots within a sensing distance Rs>RR_s > R of robot ii, so the barrier starts to act before two robots reach the safety distance (here Rs=2RR_s = 2R). On the eight robots above, with R=3R = 3 and α=0.5\alpha = 0.5:

(QP2) closest two robots over 30 s largest coordination error, last 10 s
off 0.006 0.001
on, Rs=6R_s = 6 3.110 0.253

The certificate keeps the robots apart. The price is the coordination: the robots on this spacing must dodge each other twice a lap, forever, so the coordination error never settles. The paper’s remark after (QP2) asks for exactly this: design the paths and the Δ\Delta’s so that robots at their desired spacing are further apart than RR. The certificate then only acts in the transient.

7 Step 6: fixed-wing aircraft (Theorem 3)

7.1 The model and the partial normalisation

The paper’s aircraft is a Dubins-car-like model (28): it flies at a constant speed vv, turns at a rate uθu_\theta, and climbs at a rate uzu_z:

ṗ1=vcos⁡θ,ṗ2=vsin⁡θ,ṗ3=uz,θ̇=uθ. \dot p_1 = v\cos\theta, \quad \dot p_2 = v\sin\theta, \quad \dot p_3 = u_z, \quad \dot\theta = u_\theta .

It cannot follow χ\chi as a velocity: it cannot slow down, and it cannot stop. So the field is partially normalised: scaled so that its horizontal part has the length vv. The aircraft turns towards the horizontal part, and copies the rest (29):

uz=vχ3χ12+χ22,ẇp=vχ3+pχ12+χ22. u_z = \frac{v\,\chi_3}{\sqrt{\chi_1^2 + \chi_2^2}}, \qquad \dot w_p = \frac{v\,\chi_{3+p}}{\sqrt{\chi_1^2 + \chi_2^2}} .

7.2 The heading law, and saturation

With χ̂p\hat\chi_p the direction of the horizontal part, h=(cos⁡θ,sin⁡θ)h = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta), EE the rotation by 90°90°, and σ\sigma the angle from χ̂p\hat\chi_p to hh (so h⊤Eχ̂p=sin⁡σh^\top E\hat\chi_p = \sin\sigma), the turn rate is (31)

uθ=Sat⁡ab(θ̇d−kθh⊤Eχ̂p),θ̇d=−χ̂p⊤Eχ̇p∥χp∥, u_\theta = \operatorname{Sat}_a^b\!\left(\dot\theta_d - k_\theta\, h^\top E\, \hat\chi_p\right), \qquad \dot\theta_d = -\frac{\hat\chi_p^\top E\,\dot\chi_p}{\|\chi_p\|} ,

where θ̇d\dot\theta_d (32) is the rate at which the field’s direction turns along the aircraft’s motion. It needs the derivative of the field, χ̇=Jζ̇\dot\chi = J\dot\zeta (33), and so the neighbours’ ẇ[j]\dot w^{[j]} as well as their w[j]w^{[j]}: each aircraft sends two numbers per parameter. Theorem 3: if the field’s horizontal part never vanishes and σ(0)≠π\sigma(0) \neq \pi, and if, during saturation, σ\sigma stays on the side that the saturation corrects (its Condition 2), then σ→0\sigma \to 0. Corollary 1 drops Condition 2: if |θ̇d|≤d<min⁡(−a,b)|\dot\theta_d| \le d < \min(-a, b), any kθ<k‾θ=min⁡(−a−d,b−d)k_\theta < \bar k_\theta = \min(-a - d,\ b - d) avoids saturation altogether.

What Theorem 3 gives is the heading. It does not say that the team then coordinates: once the aircraft follow the partially normalised field, robot ii’s virtual coordinate runs at v/∥χp[i]∥v/\|\chi^{[i]}_p\| times the rate of Theorem 1, and that factor differs between robots. On a path where ∥f′∥\|f'\| changes, two aircraft at the same speed and a fixed Δ≠0\Delta \neq 0 are at places where the path runs at different speeds, and they cannot both stay on it and keep the spacing. With Δ[1,2]=π/2\Delta^{[1,2]} = \pi/2 on the curve of the first flight (everything else as flown), the coordination error in the curve’s parameter βw\beta w still reaches 0.11 rad in the second half of a 20-minute flight, and the path error 23.5 m: the aircraft trade one against the other at every lap [numerical]. With Δ=0\Delta = 0, as in both flights, the issue does not arise.

On the paper’s first flight, run below in simulation, the largest |θ̇d||\dot\theta_d| once the aircraft are on the path is 0.443 rad/s. With a turn-rate limit of 0.80.8 rad/s (assumed; the paper does not give one), Corollary 1 then allows any kθk_\theta below 0.36. The paper flies kθ=1k_\theta = 1, above it, so Corollary 1 does not apply and Theorem 3 needs its Condition 2. The corollary is sufficient, not necessary: in the simulated flight the turn rate saturates in 1.2 % of the one-second records, all of them while the aircraft turn onto the path, and in 0.0 % after 300 s [numerical].

8 The program each robot runs

Before take-off, robot ii knows: its path or surface f[i]f^{[i]} and its derivatives; its gains kjk_j, kck_c; its neighbours 𝒩i\mathcal N_i and the desired differences Δ[i,j]\Delta^{[i,j]} with each of them; on a surface, the desired parametric speeds ẇ*\dot w^*.

It keeps: its virtual coordinates w[i]w^{[i]} (one per parameter), which start anywhere.

At every tick: measure its position x[i]x^{[i]}; receive w[j]w^{[j]} from each neighbour; compute ϕ=x[i]−f[i](w[i])\phi = x^{[i]} - f^{[i]}(w^{[i]}), c[i]=−∑j(w[i]−w[j]−Δ[i,j])c^{[i]} = -\sum_j (w^{[i]} - w^{[j]} - \Delta^{[i,j]}) and the field χ[i]\chi^{[i]}; move with the first nn entries; advance w[i]w^{[i]} with the last ones; send w[i]w^{[i]} to the neighbours. An aircraft also sends ẇ[i]\dot w^{[i]}, and turns with (31).

In Python, for a path, the whole on-board program is one function. The simulator calls team_field, which computes the same thing for every robot:

def program(x, w, f, df, w_nbrs, deltas, k, kc):
    """Robot i on a path: its position x (n numbers), its virtual coordinate w, its path f and f',
    what its neighbours sent (w_j) and the desired differences Delta^[i,j]. Returns its velocity and w_dot."""
    n = len(x)
    sg = 1.0 if n % 2 == 0 else -1.0
    fx, dfx = f(w), df(w)
    phi = [x[j] - fx[j] for j in range(n)]
    c = -sum((w - wj) - d for wj, d in zip(w_nbrs, deltas))
    u = [sg * dfx[j] - k[j] * phi[j] for j in range(n)]
    w_dot = sg + sum(k[j] * phi[j] * dfx[j] for j in range(n)) + kc * c
    return u, w_dot

At the example’s start, the 21 programs and the simulator’s field differ by 0.0e+00.

9 The simulator

The world, not the robots: Euler ticks with the commands held for one tick. For a single integrator a held command is exact physics; the path error then settles at a small floor set by the tick, which halves when the tick halves. The aircraft use the same ticks for (28). The box below holds the complete core of this page (click to open it).

Notecore.py: the core of this page (click to open; the JavaScript of the figures is a line-by-line port) 
"""The Python core of the paper's pages: every number the explainer prints is computed here, at render time.

Paper: W. Yao, H. Garcia de Marina, Z. Sun, M. Cao, "Guiding vector fields for the distributed motion coordination
of mobile robots", IEEE Transactions on Robotics 39(2), 2023 (multi_jrn_main.tex in the folder above).

A line-by-line twin of assets/core.js: same functions, same names, same order of operations. `make check` runs
check() here and EX.core.check() in deno, and compares every value (1e-9). Plain Python (math, lists), no numpy, so
that the port is exact. A robot's generalised coordinate is xi = (x_1, ..., x_n, w_1, ..., w_k): its position in R^n
and its k virtual coordinates (k = 1 for a path, k = 2 for a surface), the virtual ones last, as in the paper.
"""
import math


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a seeded generator, identical in both languages
class Rng:
    """xorshift32, and a Gaussian by Box-Muller (EX.core.Rng in the JavaScript)."""

    def __init__(self, seed):
        self.s = (seed & 0xFFFFFFFF) or 1

    def u(self):
        s = self.s
        s ^= (s << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        s ^= s >> 17
        s ^= (s << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        self.s = s
        return s / 4294967296

    def n(self):
        a = self.u()
        b = self.u()
        return math.sqrt(-2 * math.log(1 - a)) * math.cos(2 * math.pi * b)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ paths (k = 1) and surfaces (k = 2)
def shape(kind, **p):
    """A parametric path or surface. Paths: circle (a), ellipse (a, b), eight3d (the paper's first simulation),
    lissajous (c_j cos(om_j w + d_j) + m_j on each axis). Surfaces: sphere (r), torus (R, r; tube = 0 when w_1 is the
    angle around the tube, as in the fourth simulation, tube = 1 when it is w_2, as in the flight). o: an offset."""
    S = {"kind": kind, "o": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]}
    S.update(p)
    S["n"] = 2 if kind in ("circle", "ellipse") else 3
    S["k"] = 2 if kind in ("sphere", "torus") else 1
    return S


def shape_eval(S, w):
    """f(w), its first derivatives d[p] = df/dw_p and its second derivatives dd[p][q], each a list of n numbers. With
    a scale beta (as in the flight code), the shape is f(beta_1 w_1, beta_2 w_2) and the derivatives follow."""
    be = S.get("beta")
    if be is None:
        return shape_raw(S, w)
    f, d, dd = shape_raw(S, [w[p] * be[p] for p in range(len(w))])
    k = len(w)
    d = [[x * be[p] for x in d[p]] for p in range(k)]
    dd = [[[x * be[p] * be[q] for x in dd[p][q]] for q in range(k)] for p in range(k)]
    return f, d, dd


def shape_raw(S, w):
    """f(w), its first derivatives d[p] = df/dw_p and its second derivatives dd[p][q], each a list of n numbers."""
    kd = S["kind"]
    if kd == "circle" or kd == "ellipse":
        a = S["a"]
        b = S["b"] if kd == "ellipse" else S["a"]
        c, s = math.cos(w[0]), math.sin(w[0])
        f = [a * c, b * s]
        d = [[-a * s, b * c]]
        dd = [[[-a * c, -b * s]]]
    elif kd == "eight3d":
        # x = 15 sin 2w, y = 30 sin w sqrt(0.5 (1 - 0.5 sin^2 w)), z = 5 + 5 cos 2w - 2
        s, c = math.sin(w[0]), math.cos(w[0])
        q = 0.5 - 0.25 * s * s
        r = math.sqrt(q)
        y = 30 * s * r
        yd = 30 * c * r - 7.5 * s * s * c / r
        ydd = (-30 * s * r - 7.5 * s * c * c / r
               - 7.5 * (2 * s * c * c / r - s * s * s / r + 0.25 * s * s * s * c * c / (r * q)))
        s2, c2 = math.sin(2 * w[0]), math.cos(2 * w[0])
        f = [15 * s2, y, 3 + 5 * c2]
        d = [[30 * c2, yd, -10 * s2]]
        dd = [[[-60 * s2, ydd, -20 * c2]]]
    elif kd == "lissajous":
        f, d0, dd0 = [], [], []
        for j in range(3):
            c, om, ph = S["c"][j], S["om"][j], S["d"][j]
            f.append(c * math.cos(om * w[0] + ph) + S["m"][j])
            d0.append(-c * om * math.sin(om * w[0] + ph))
            dd0.append(-c * om * om * math.cos(om * w[0] + ph))
        d = [d0]
        dd = [[dd0]]
    elif kd == "sphere":
        r = S["r"]
        c1, s1, c2, s2 = math.cos(w[0]), math.sin(w[0]), math.cos(w[1]), math.sin(w[1])
        f = [r * c1 * c2, r * c1 * s2, r * s1]
        d = [[-r * s1 * c2, -r * s1 * s2, r * c1], [-r * c1 * s2, r * c1 * c2, 0.0]]
        dd = [[[-r * c1 * c2, -r * c1 * s2, -r * s1], [r * s1 * s2, -r * s1 * c2, 0.0]],
              [[r * s1 * s2, -r * s1 * c2, 0.0], [-r * c1 * c2, -r * c1 * s2, 0.0]]]
    elif kd == "torus":
        R, r = S["R"], S["r"]
        a, b = (w[0], w[1]) if S.get("tube", 0) == 0 else (w[1], w[0])     # a: around the tube, b: around the axis
        ca, sa, cb, sb = math.cos(a), math.sin(a), math.cos(b), math.sin(b)
        rho = R + r * ca
        f = [rho * cb, rho * sb, r * sa]
        da = [-r * sa * cb, -r * sa * sb, r * ca]
        db = [-rho * sb, rho * cb, 0.0]
        daa = [-r * ca * cb, -r * ca * sb, -r * sa]
        dab = [r * sa * sb, -r * sa * cb, 0.0]
        dbb = [-rho * cb, -rho * sb, 0.0]
        if S.get("tube", 0) == 0:
            d, dd = [da, db], [[daa, dab], [dab, dbb]]
        else:
            d, dd = [db, da], [[dbb, dab], [dab, daa]]
    else:
        raise ValueError(kd)
    f = [f[j] + S["o"][j] for j in range(len(f))]
    return f, d, dd


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the coordinating guiding vector field
def field(S, xi, kg, ws, c, kc):
    """chi^[i] of robot i: (5) = (3) + k_c (4) for a path, (17) = (15) + k_c1 (16a) + k_c2 (16b) for a surface, with the
    extra vector v of Theorem 2, v = (-1)^(n+1) (0, ..., 0, ws_2, -ws_1). kg: the gains k_j (n of them); ws: the
    desired parametric speeds (surfaces only); c: the coordination functions (7) or (19), already evaluated; kc: their
    gains. Returns chi and the errors phi_j = x_j - f_j(w)."""
    n, k = S["n"], S["k"]
    f, d, dd = shape_eval(S, xi[n:])
    phi = [xi[j] - f[j] for j in range(n)]
    sg = 1.0 if n % 2 == 0 else -1.0
    chi = [0.0] * (n + k)
    if k == 1:
        s = 0.0
        for j in range(n):
            chi[j] = sg * d[0][j] - kg[j] * phi[j]
            s += kg[j] * phi[j] * d[0][j]
        chi[n] = sg + s + kc[0] * c[0]
    else:
        v1 = -sg * ws[1]          # v_{n+1} = (-1)^(n+1) ws_2
        v2 = sg * ws[0]           # v_{n+2} = (-1)^(n+1) (-ws_1)
        s1, s2 = 0.0, 0.0
        for j in range(n):
            chi[j] = sg * (v2 * d[0][j] - v1 * d[1][j]) - kg[j] * phi[j]
            s1 += kg[j] * phi[j] * d[0][j]
            s2 += kg[j] * phi[j] * d[1][j]
        chi[n] = sg * v2 + s1 + kc[0] * c[0]
        chi[n + 1] = -sg * v1 + s2 + kc[1] * c[1]
    return chi, phi


def nominal_speed(S, ws):
    """The parametric speed on the path or surface: (-1)^n for a path, ws for a surface (Theorem 2)."""
    if S["k"] == 1:
        return [1.0 if S["n"] % 2 == 0 else -1.0]
    return [ws[0], ws[1]]


def coordination(W, Wstar, nbrs, i):
    """(7) or (19) for robot i: c_p = -sum_j (w_p^[i] - w_p^[j] - Delta_p^[i,j]), Delta^[i,j] = w*^[i] - w*^[j]."""
    k = len(W[i])
    c = [0.0] * k
    for j in nbrs[i]:
        for p in range(k):
            c[p] -= (W[i][p] - W[j][p]) - (Wstar[i][p] - Wstar[j][p])
    return c


def cycle(N):
    """The cycle graph C_N of the paper's simulations: robot i talks to i - 1 and i + 1."""
    if N == 1:
        return [[]]
    if N == 2:
        return [[1], [0]]
    return [[(i - 1) % N, (i + 1) % N] for i in range(N)]


def team(shapes, nbrs, wstar, kg, kc, ws=None):
    """A team: one shape per robot, the graph (lists of neighbours), the reference w* (a list of k numbers per robot),
    the gains k_j (one list per robot), k_c (k numbers) and the desired parametric speeds (surfaces)."""
    return {"S": shapes, "N": nbrs, "ws_ref": wstar, "kg": kg, "kc": kc, "ws": ws or [0.0, 0.0]}


def team_field(T, X):
    """The commands of every robot (single integrators: xi_dot = chi), and their errors phi."""
    Nr = len(X)
    W = [X[i][T["S"][i]["n"]:] for i in range(Nr)]
    out, phis = [], []
    for i in range(Nr):
        c = coordination(W, T["ws_ref"], T["N"], i)
        chi, phi = field(T["S"][i], X[i], T["kg"][i], T["ws"], c, T["kc"])
        out.append(chi)
        phis.append(phi)
    return out, phis


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ collision avoidance: (QP2), each robot on its own
def safety_filter(T, X, chis, sf):
    """(QP2) for every robot: the closest command to chi^[i] with (xi^[j] - xi^[i])^T P^T chi <= alpha/4 h_ij^3 for
    j in D_i, h_ij = |P (xi^[i] - xi^[j])|^2 - R^2, and D_i the robots within the sensing distance Rs. Solved by
    Hildreth's method, a fixed number of sweeps. P keeps the position and drops the virtual coordinates."""
    Nr = len(X)
    R2, al = sf["R"] * sf["R"], sf["alpha"]
    lim = sf["Rs"] * sf["Rs"]
    out = []
    active = 0
    for i in range(Nr):
        n = T["S"][i]["n"]
        A, B = [], []
        for j in range(Nr):
            if j == i:
                continue
            a = [X[j][l] - X[i][l] for l in range(n)]
            d2 = 0.0
            for l in range(n):
                d2 += a[l] * a[l]
            if d2 <= lim and d2 > 1e-18:
                h = d2 - R2
                A.append(a)
                B.append(al / 4 * h * h * h)
        y = chis[i][:]
        lam = [0.0] * len(A)
        for sweep in range(40):
            for m in range(len(A)):
                aa, ay = 0.0, 0.0
                for l in range(n):
                    aa += A[m][l] * A[m][l]
                    ay += A[m][l] * y[l]
                new = lam[m] + (ay - B[m]) / aa
                if new < 0:
                    new = 0.0
                dl = new - lam[m]
                lam[m] = new
                for l in range(n):
                    y[l] -= dl * A[m][l]
        for m in range(len(A)):
            if lam[m] > 0:
                active += 1
        out.append(y)
    return out, active


def step(T, X, dt, sf=None, held=None):
    """The world: one Euler tick of xi_dot = chi (or the filtered chi), commands held for the tick. A held robot does
    not move; its virtual coordinates still run (its program runs). Returns the new state and the commands."""
    chis, phis = team_field(T, X)
    if sf is not None:
        chis, _ = safety_filter(T, X, chis, sf)
    Xn = []
    for i in range(len(X)):
        n = T["S"][i]["n"]
        q = X[i][:]
        for l in range(len(q)):
            if held is not None and held[i] and l < n:
                continue
            q[l] += dt * chis[i][l]
        Xn.append(q)
    return Xn, chis


def simulate(T, X0, dt, steps, every=1, sf=None):
    """Euler ticks of the team; the states every `every` ticks (the first one included)."""
    X = [x[:] for x in X0]
    out = [X]
    for s in range(1, steps + 1):
        X, _ = step(T, X, dt, sf)
        if s % every == 0:
            out.append(X)
    return out


def errors(T, X):
    """The objectives of Problems 1 and 2: the largest |Phi^[i]|, and the largest coordination error over the
    edges, |w_p^[i] - w_p^[j] - Delta_p^[i,j]|."""
    Nr = len(X)
    _, phis = team_field(T, X)
    ep = 0.0
    for phi in phis:
        s = 0.0
        for v in phi:
            s += v * v
        ep = max(ep, math.sqrt(s))
    ec = 0.0
    for i in range(Nr):
        ni = T["S"][i]["n"]
        for j in T["N"][i]:
            nj = T["S"][j]["n"]
            for p in range(T["S"][i]["k"]):
                e = (X[i][ni + p] - X[j][nj + p]) - (T["ws_ref"][i][p] - T["ws_ref"][j][p])
                ec = max(ec, abs(e))
    return ep, ec


def lyapunov(T, X):
    """V of the proofs, (41) and (55) (V = 1/2 (Phi^T K Phi + k_c w~^T L w~), the sum running over the k parameters), and
    its derivative as the proofs write it, (45) and (59): -|K Phi|^2 - sum_p |F_p^T K Phi - k_cp L w~_p|^2. The p-th
    entry of robot i in the last term is chi_{n+p}^[i] - (the nominal parametric speed), which is how it is computed
    here."""
    Nr = len(X)
    chis, phis = team_field(T, X)
    V, Vd = 0.0, 0.0
    for i in range(Nr):
        S = T["S"][i]
        n = S["n"]
        for j in range(n):
            kp = T["kg"][i][j] * phis[i][j]
            V += 0.5 * kp * phis[i][j]
            Vd -= kp * kp
        om = nominal_speed(S, T["ws"])
        for p in range(S["k"]):
            r = chis[i][n + p] - om[p]
            Vd -= r * r
            for j in T["N"][i]:
                if j > i:
                    nj = T["S"][j]["n"]
                    e = (X[i][n + p] - X[j][nj + p]) - (T["ws_ref"][i][p] - T["ws_ref"][j][p])
                    V += 0.5 * T["kc"][p] * e * e
    return V, Vd


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the Dubins-car-like aircraft, Section V
def field_jac(S, xi, kg, ws, kc, deg):
    """The Jacobian of chi^[i] with respect to the robot's own (x, w): (25) of the paper for a surface in R^3, the
    same construction for a path. The coordination part on w^[i] is -k_c deg_i; the part on the neighbours' w is
    handled through c_dot by the caller. Written from the field above, with each row's own gain k_j."""
    n, k = S["n"], S["k"]
    f, d, dd = shape_eval(S, xi[n:])
    phi = [xi[j] - f[j] for j in range(n)]
    om = nominal_speed(S, ws)
    J = [[0.0] * (n + k) for _ in range(n + k)]
    for j in range(n):
        J[j][j] = -kg[j]
        for q in range(k):
            s = 0.0
            for p in range(k):
                s += om[p] * dd[p][q][j]
            J[j][n + q] = s + kg[j] * d[q][j]
    for p in range(k):
        for l in range(n):
            J[n + p][l] = kg[l] * d[p][l]
        for q in range(k):
            s = 0.0
            for j in range(n):
                s += kg[j] * (phi[j] * dd[p][q][j] - d[q][j] * d[p][j])
            J[n + p][n + q] = s
        J[n + p][n + p] -= kc[p] * deg
    return J


def sat(x, m):
    return x if m <= 0 else max(-m, min(m, x))


def air_commands(A, st, wind):
    """One tick of the program of every aircraft (Theorem 3, (29) and (31)). Each robot measures its own position (with
    its GPS bias), its ground velocity g and course, and its virtual coordinates, and hears its neighbours' w and
    w_dot. Phase 1, from positions and w alone: chi, w_dot = |g| chi_w / |chi_12| and u_z = |g| chi_3 / |chi_12|.
    Phase 2, with the neighbours' w_dot: chi_dot = J zeta_dot, the turn rate theta_d_dot of the field's course (32),
    and u_theta (31). Without wind |g| = v and the course is theta, the paper's model (28); the flight code also uses
    the measured ground speed and course."""
    T, v = A["T"], A["v"]
    Nr = len(st)
    X, G = [], []
    for i in range(Nr):
        b = A["bias"][i]
        X.append([st[i]["x"][l] + b[l] for l in range(len(st[i]["x"]))] + st[i]["w"])
        G.append([v * math.cos(st[i]["th"]) + wind[0], v * math.sin(st[i]["th"]) + wind[1]])
    chis, phis = team_field(T, X)
    cmd = []
    for i in range(Nr):
        n = T["S"][i]["n"]
        chi = chis[i]
        gs = math.sqrt(G[i][0] * G[i][0] + G[i][1] * G[i][1])
        nh = math.sqrt(chi[0] * chi[0] + chi[1] * chi[1])
        wd = [gs * chi[n + p] / nh for p in range(T["S"][i]["k"])]
        uz = gs * chi[2] / nh if n == 3 else 0.0
        cmd.append({"chi": chi, "phi": phis[i], "wd": wd, "uz": uz, "nh": nh})
    for i in range(Nr):
        S = T["S"][i]
        n, k = S["n"], S["k"]
        chi = chis[i]
        gs = math.sqrt(G[i][0] * G[i][0] + G[i][1] * G[i][1])
        hc, hs = G[i][0] / gs, G[i][1] / gs
        zd = [G[i][0], G[i][1]] + ([cmd[i]["uz"]] if n == 3 else []) + cmd[i]["wd"]
        J = field_jac(S, X[i], T["kg"][i], T["ws"], T["kc"], len(T["N"][i]))
        cd = [0.0] * (n + k)
        for r in range(n + k):
            s = 0.0
            for q in range(n + k):
                s += J[r][q] * zd[q]
            cd[r] = s
        for p in range(k):                       # the neighbours' part of c_dot: + k_c sum_j w_dot_p^[j]
            for j in T["N"][i]:
                cd[n + p] += T["kc"][p] * cmd[j]["wd"][p]
        nc = 0.0
        for r in range(n + k):
            nc += chi[r] * chi[r]
        nc = math.sqrt(nc)
        ch = [x / nc for x in chi]
        cJ = 0.0
        for r in range(n + k):
            cJ += ch[r] * cd[r]
        p0, p1 = ch[0], ch[1]
        pd0, pd1 = (cd[0] - ch[0] * cJ) / nc, (cd[1] - ch[1] * cJ) / nc
        g2 = p0 * p0 + p1 * p1
        thd = (p0 * pd1 - p1 * pd0) / g2
        ng = math.sqrt(g2)
        hEg = hc * (-p1 / ng) + hs * (p0 / ng)          # h^T E chi_p_hat = sin(sigma)
        cmd[i]["thd"] = thd
        cmd[i]["sig"] = math.atan2(hEg, hc * (p0 / ng) + hs * (p1 / ng))
        raw = thd - A["kth"] * hEg
        cmd[i]["ut"] = sat(raw, A["umax"])
        cmd[i]["sat"] = 1.0 if (A["umax"] > 0 and abs(raw) > A["umax"]) else 0.0
    return cmd


def air_tick(A, st, cmd, dt, wind):
    """The world: one Euler tick of (28) with the commands held, plus a constant wind the program does not know."""
    v = A["v"]
    out = []
    for i in range(len(st)):
        x = st[i]["x"][:]
        th = st[i]["th"]
        x[0] += dt * (v * math.cos(th) + wind[0])
        x[1] += dt * (v * math.sin(th) + wind[1])
        if len(x) == 3:
            x[2] += dt * cmd[i]["uz"]
        out.append({"x": x, "th": th + dt * cmd[i]["ut"], "w": [st[i]["w"][p] + dt * cmd[i]["wd"][p] for p in range(len(st[i]["w"]))]})
    return out


def fly(A, st0, dt, steps, every=1, wind=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Fly the team of aircraft. Returns the samples: states, and the largest |theta_d_dot|, |sigma| and saturation."""
    st = [{"x": s["x"][:], "th": s["th"], "w": s["w"][:]} for s in st0]
    out = [{"st": st, "t": 0.0}]
    for s in range(1, steps + 1):
        cmd = air_commands(A, st, wind)
        st = air_tick(A, st, cmd, dt, wind)
        if s % every == 0:
            out.append({"st": st, "t": s * dt, "thd": [c["thd"] for c in cmd], "sig": [c["sig"] for c in cmd],
                        "sat": [c["sat"] for c in cmd], "phi": [c["phi"] for c in cmd]})
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ starts, references and patterns
def scatter(T, rng, spread, wspread, centre=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)):
    """Random starts: positions with Gaussian spread around a centre, virtual coordinates with Gaussian spread."""
    X = []
    for S in T["S"]:
        q = [centre[l] + spread * rng.n() for l in range(S["n"])]
        q += [wspread * rng.n() for _ in range(S["k"])]
        X.append(q)
    return X


def even_ref(N, span):
    """w*^[i] = (i - 1) span / N: the references of the paper's simulations (span = T/2 = pi in the first one,
    2 pi in the second and the third)."""
    return [[i * span / N] for i in range(N)]


# a stroke font for patterns on a surface: each letter a list of polylines in a box 0..1 (x) by 0..1.4 (y)
GLYPHS = {
    "G": [[[0.95, 1.15], [0.75, 1.38], [0.3, 1.38], [0.05, 1.1], [0.05, 0.3], [0.3, 0.02], [0.75, 0.02], [0.95, 0.3], [0.95, 0.65], [0.55, 0.65]]],
    "V": [[[0.0, 1.4], [0.5, 0.0], [1.0, 1.4]]],
    "F": [[[0.9, 1.4], [0.05, 1.4], [0.05, 0.0]], [[0.05, 0.72], [0.7, 0.72]]],
}


def pattern(text, step, w1c, w2c, h, aspect=1.0):
    """Points along the strokes of `text`, one every `step` of arc length, as references (w*_1, w*_2) on a surface:
    the letters read along w_2 (around the torus) and stand along w_1 (around the tube), height h, centred on
    (w1c, w2c). aspect shrinks the letters along w_2 (1/3 on a torus three times wider around its axis than around
    its tube, so that they keep their shape in space). The cycle graph joins the points in the order they are drawn."""
    pts = []
    x0 = 0.0
    for ch in text:
        for line in GLYPHS[ch]:
            carry = 0.0
            for a in range(len(line) - 1):
                p, q = line[a], line[a + 1]
                L = math.sqrt((q[0] - p[0]) ** 2 + (q[1] - p[1]) ** 2)
                t = carry
                while t <= L + 1e-12:
                    c = [x0 + p[0] + (q[0] - p[0]) * t / L, p[1] + (q[1] - p[1]) * t / L]
                    near = False
                    for r in pts:                 # a corner can give a point twice: keep the first
                        if (r[0] - c[0]) ** 2 + (r[1] - c[1]) ** 2 < 0.25 * step * step:
                            near = True
                    if not near:
                        pts.append(c)
                    t += step
                carry = t - L
        x0 += 1.45
    W = x0 - 0.45
    s = h / 1.4
    return [[w1c + (y - 0.7) * s, w2c + (x - W / 2) * s * aspect] for x, y in pts]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a census of random teams for Theorem 1
def random_team(rng, graph="connected", delta="feasible"):
    """A random team in the plane, for Theorem 1: 3 to 8 robots, each on its own ellipse (half-axes 2 to 10, centre
    within 5), gains k_j in [0.3, 3] and k_c in [0.3, 10], references w* in [-pi, pi]. graph: "connected" (a random
    tree plus random chords), "two parts" (the same, cut in two). delta: "feasible" (from w*), or "ring" (a cycle
    graph where every edge asks for 2 pi / N, which cannot close around the cycle)."""
    N = 3 + int(rng.u() * 6)
    shapes = []
    for i in range(N):
        a, b = 2 + 8 * rng.u(), 2 + 8 * rng.u()
        shapes.append(shape("ellipse", a=a, b=b, o=[10 * rng.u() - 5, 10 * rng.u() - 5, 0.0]))
    nb = [[] for _ in range(N)]
    if delta == "ring":
        nb = cycle(N)
    else:
        cut = N // 2 if graph == "two parts" else 0
        for i in range(1, N):
            if i == cut:
                continue
            lo = cut if i > cut else 0
            j = lo + int(rng.u() * (i - lo))
            nb[i].append(j)
            nb[j].append(i)
        for i in range(N):
            for j in range(i + 1, N):
                same = (i < cut) == (j < cut) if cut else True
                if same and j not in nb[i] and rng.u() < 0.2:
                    nb[i].append(j)
                    nb[j].append(i)
    kg = [[0.3 + 2.7 * rng.u(), 0.3 + 2.7 * rng.u()] for _ in range(N)]
    kc = [0.3 + 9.7 * rng.u()]
    ref = [[math.pi * (2 * rng.u() - 1)] for _ in range(N)]
    T = team(shapes, nb, ref, kg, kc)
    if delta == "ring":
        T["ring"] = 2 * math.pi / N
        T["ws_ref"] = [[-i * T["ring"]] for i in range(N)]       # every edge (i, i+1) asks for 2 pi / N ...
    return T


def ring_errors(T, X):
    """The coordination error of the "ring" census: every edge (i, i + 1 mod N) asks w^[i] - w^[i+1] = 2 pi / N."""
    N = len(X)
    ec = 0.0
    for i in range(N):
        j = (i + 1) % N
        ec = max(ec, abs((X[i][2] - X[j][2]) - T["ring"]))
    return ec


def ring_coordination(W, T, i):
    """(7) with the inconsistent ring of desired differences: Delta^[i,i+1] = 2 pi / N = -Delta^[i+1,i]."""
    N = len(W)
    c = [0.0]
    c[0] -= (W[i][0] - W[(i + 1) % N][0]) - T["ring"]
    c[0] -= (W[i][0] - W[(i - 1) % N][0]) + T["ring"]
    return c


def census_run(T, rng, tend, spread):
    """One member of the census: a start far from everything, Euler ticks small enough for the stiffest robot, and
    the record of V every 0.5 s. Returns [largest |Phi|, largest edge error, largest rise of V between two records
    (as a fraction of V at the start), ticks]."""
    N = len(T["S"])
    X = []
    for i in range(N):
        X.append([spread * (2 * rng.u() - 1), spread * (2 * rng.u() - 1), 10 * (2 * rng.u() - 1)])
    stiff = 0.0
    for i in range(N):
        S = T["S"][i]
        fm = max(S["a"], S["b"])
        stiff = max(stiff, max(T["kg"][i]) * (1 + fm * fm) + 2 * T["kc"][0] * len(T["N"][i]))
    dt = min(2e-3, 0.4 / stiff)
    steps = int(tend / dt + 0.5)
    every = max(1, int(0.5 / dt + 0.5))
    rise = 0.0
    ring = "ring" in T
    Vp, V0 = None, None
    for s in range(steps + 1):
        if s % every == 0 and not ring:
            V, _ = lyapunov(T, X)
            if V0 is None:
                V0 = V
            if Vp is not None:
                rise = max(rise, (V - Vp) / V0)
            Vp = V
        if s == steps:
            break
        if ring:
            W = [x[2:] for x in X]
            Xn = []
            for i in range(N):
                c = ring_coordination(W, T, i)
                chi, _ = field(T["S"][i], X[i], T["kg"][i], T["ws"], c, T["kc"])
                Xn.append([X[i][l] + dt * chi[l] for l in range(3)])
            X = Xn
        else:
            X, _ = step(T, X, dt)
    ep, ec = errors(T, X)
    if ring:
        ec = ring_errors(T, X)
    return [ep, ec, rise, steps]


def census(M, seed, graph="connected", delta="feasible", tend=20.0, spread=50.0):
    """M random teams from one seed: per team [N, largest |Phi|, largest edge error, largest rise of V] at tend."""
    rng = Rng(seed)
    out = []
    for m in range(M):
        T = random_team(rng, graph, delta)
        r = census_run(T, rng, tend, spread)
        out.append([len(T["S"]), r[0], r[1], r[2]])
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the paper's simulations and flights (Section VI)
def sim1_team(N=50):
    """The first simulation (Fig. 3): N robots on the bent figure eight in R^3, k_j = 1, k_c = 300, w*^[i] = (i - 1)
    T/(2N)."""
    S = shape("eight3d")
    return team([S] * N, cycle(N), even_ref(N, math.pi), [[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]] * N, [300.0])


def sim2_team(N=3):
    """The second simulation (Fig. 4): the open Lissajous curve with irrational coefficients, k_j = k_c = 1."""
    S = shape("lissajous", c=[1.0, 1.0, 1.0], om=[math.sqrt(2), 4.1, 7.1], d=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], m=[0.1, 0.7, 0.0])
    return team([S] * N, cycle(N), even_ref(N, 2 * math.pi), [[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]] * N, [1.0])


def sim3_team(N=21, a=10.0, b=5.0, kc=100.0):
    """The third simulation (Fig. 5): three concentric paths, seven robots each (a large circle, an ellipse, a small
    circle), k_j = 1, k_c = 100, w*^[i] = (i - 1) 2 pi / N."""
    big, ell, small = shape("circle", a=a), shape("ellipse", a=a, b=b), shape("circle", a=b)
    m = N // 3
    shapes = [big] * m + [ell] * m + [small] * (N - 2 * m)
    return team(shapes, cycle(N), even_ref(N, 2 * math.pi), [[1.0, 1.0]] * N, [kc])


def sim4_team(ref, kc=10.0, ws=(-1.0, -1.0)):
    """The fourth simulation (Fig. 6): robots on the torus (2 + cos w1) cos w2, (2 + cos w1) sin w2, sin w1, references
    from a pattern, k_j = 1, k_c = 10, desired parametric speeds -1 and -1 (so v = (0, 0, 0, -1, 1))."""
    S = shape("torus", R=2.0, r=1.0, tube=0)
    N = len(ref)
    return team([S] * N, cycle(N), ref, [[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]] * N, [kc, kc], list(ws))


def example2_team(ws):
    """Example 2 (Fig. 1): two robots on the unit sphere, Delta_1 = Delta_2 = -pi."""
    S = shape("sphere", r=1.0)
    return team([S, S], cycle(2), [[0.0, 0.0], [math.pi, math.pi]], [[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]] * 2, [1.0, 1.0], list(ws))


def flight1(bias=1.0, delta=0.0):
    """The first flight (Figs. 7 and 8): two aircraft on the Lissajous curve 225 cos w, 225 cos(2 w + pi/2), -20 cos 2 w,
    rendezvous (Delta = 0), k = 0.002, 0.002, 0.0025, k_c = 0.01, k_theta = 1, on the scaled field the paper states for
    the flights, phi = L (x - f(beta w)) with L = 0.1 and beta = 0.01 (the consensus term added after the scaling, on
    beta w). In the field (3) that is the path f(beta w) with gains k / L, k_c beta / L^3 and Delta / beta. The second
    aircraft's GPS is biased by 1 m in the horizontal plane. The airspeed (12 m/s) and the turn-rate limit (0.8 rad/s)
    are not in the paper."""
    L, be = 0.1, 0.01
    S = shape("lissajous", c=[225.0, 225.0, -20.0], om=[1.0, 2.0, 2.0], d=[0.0, math.pi / 2, 0.0], m=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    S["beta"] = [be]
    kg, kc, ref = [0.002 / L, 0.002 / L, 0.0025 / L], [0.01 * be / L ** 3], [[0.0], [delta / be]]
    T = team([S, S], cycle(2), ref, [kg, kg], kc)
    return {"T": T, "v": 12.0, "kth": 1.0, "umax": 0.8, "bias": [[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [bias, 0.0, 0.0]]}


def flight2(bias=1.0):
    """The second flight (Figs. 10 and 11): two aircraft on the torus (100 + 5 cos w2) cos w1, (100 + 5 cos w2) sin w1,
    5 sin w2 + 50, rendezvous, k = 0.003, k_c1 = k_c2 = 0.01, k_theta = 1, on the scaled field with L = 0.1 and the
    parameter scalings beta_1 = 0.005, beta_2 = 0.01 that set w2* dot = 2 w1* dot (the field (15) for f(beta_1 w_1,
    beta_2 w_2) with parametric speeds one, gains k / L and k_cp beta_p / L^3)."""
    L = 0.1
    S = shape("torus", R=100.0, r=5.0, tube=1, o=[0.0, 0.0, 50.0])
    S["beta"] = [0.005, 0.01]
    kg, kc, ws = [0.003 / L] * 3, [0.01 * 0.005 / L ** 3, 0.01 * 0.01 / L ** 3], [1.0, 1.0]
    T = team([S, S], cycle(2), [[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]], [kg, kg], kc, ws)
    return {"T": T, "v": 12.0, "kth": 1.0, "umax": 0.8, "bias": [[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [bias, 0.0, 0.0]]}


def check():
    """The same keys as EX.core.check() in assets/core.js."""
    out = {}
    r = Rng(7)
    out["rng"] = [r.u(), r.u(), r.n()]
    shapes = [shape("circle", a=2.0), shape("ellipse", a=10.0, b=5.0), shape("eight3d"), sim2_team()["S"][0],
              shape("sphere", r=1.0), shape("torus", R=2.0, r=1.0), shape("torus", R=100.0, r=5.0, tube=1, o=[0.0, 0.0, 50.0])]
    ev = []
    for S in shapes:
        w = [0.7, -1.3][:S["k"]]
        f, d, dd = shape_eval(S, w)
        ev += f + [x for row in d for x in row] + [x for a in dd for b in a for x in b]
    out["shapes"] = ev
    chi, phi = field(shapes[2], [1.0, -2.0, 0.5, 0.3], [1.0, 2.0, 0.5], [0, 0], [0.4], [3.0])
    out["field_path"] = chi + phi
    chi, phi = field(shapes[5], [1.0, -2.0, 0.5, 0.3, 2.0], [1.0, 2.0, 0.5], [-1.0, 0.5], [0.4, -0.2], [3.0, 2.0])
    out["field_surf"] = chi + phi
    out["jac"] = [x for row in field_jac(shapes[5], [1.0, -2.0, 0.5, 0.3, 2.0], [1.0, 2.0, 0.5], [-1.0, 0.5], [3.0, 2.0], 2) for x in row]
    T = sim3_team(6, 10.0, 5.0, 20.0)
    X0 = scatter(T, Rng(11), 6.0, 2.0)
    run = simulate(T, X0, 1e-3, 3000, 1000)
    out["sim3"] = [x for X in run for q in X for x in q]
    out["errors"] = list(errors(T, run[-1])) + list(lyapunov(T, run[0])) + list(lyapunov(T, run[-1]))
    T2 = example2_team([1.0, 1.0])
    run = simulate(T2, [[0.5, 0.2, 1.1, 0.0, 0.0], [-1.2, 0.4, -0.3, 1.0, 2.0]], 1e-3, 2000, 1000)
    out["sphere"] = [x for X in run for q in X for x in q]
    T3 = team([shape("eight3d")] * 4, cycle(4), even_ref(4, 2 * math.pi), [[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]] * 4, [5.0])
    X3 = [list(shape_eval(T3["S"][0], [w[0]])[0]) + [w[0]] for w in T3["ws_ref"]]
    sf = {"R": 3.0, "alpha": 0.5, "mode": "range", "Rs": 6.0}
    chis, _ = team_field(T3, [[x + 0.1 * (i + 1) for x in q] for i, q in enumerate(X3)])
    filt, act = safety_filter(T3, [[x + 0.1 * (i + 1) for x in q] for i, q in enumerate(X3)], chis, sf)
    out["qp"] = [x for q in filt for x in q] + [act]
    run = simulate(T3, X3, 2e-3, 600, 300, {"R": 3.0, "alpha": 0.5, "mode": "range", "Rs": 4.0})
    out["safe_run"] = [x for X in run for q in X for x in q]
    A = flight1()
    st0 = [{"x": [-150.0, 60.0, 10.0], "th": 0.3, "w": [0.0]}, {"x": [100.0, -40.0, -5.0], "th": 2.0, "w": [1.0]}]
    fl = fly(A, st0, 0.1, 300, 100, (1.0, -2.0))
    out["fly"] = [x for s in fl for q in s["st"] for x in q["x"] + [q["th"]] + q["w"]] + [fl[-1]["thd"][0], fl[-1]["sig"][1]]
    A2 = flight2()
    st2 = [{"x": [90.0, 10.0, 48.0], "th": 1.5, "w": [0.1, 0.0]}, {"x": [-20.0, 99.0, 55.0], "th": 3.0, "w": [1.7, 1.0]}]
    fl = fly(A2, st2, 0.1, 200, 100)
    out["fly2"] = [x for s in fl for q in s["st"] for x in q["x"] + [q["th"]] + q["w"]]
    out["pattern"] = [x for q in pattern("GVF", 0.5, 0.0, 1.0, 1.6) for x in q]
    out["census"] = [x for r in census(2, 5, "connected", "feasible", 1.0, 20.0) + census(1, 6, "two parts", "feasible", 1.0, 20.0)
                     + census(1, 7, "connected", "ring", 1.0, 20.0) for x in r]
    return out

10 Running it: the paper’s simulations again

The paper does not give its starting positions; the ones below are ours (seeded, Gaussian). Everything else is the paper’s.

10.1 Fig. 1: two robots on the sphere

In both scenarios the robots reach the sphere and run as Fig. 1 shows: along two parallels mirrored across the equator for ẇ*=(0,1)\dot w^* = (0, 1), and along two winding curves for ẇ*=(1,1)\dot w^* = (1, 1). Both robots’ parametric speeds end at ẇ*\dot w^*.

10.2 Fig. 3: 50 robots on the bent figure eight

The first simulation: 50 robots on

x=(15sin2w,30sinw0.5(1−0.5sin⁡2w),3+5cos2w), x = \left(15\sin 2w,\ \ 30\sin w\sqrt{0.5\,(1 - 0.5\sin^2 w)},\ \ 3 + 5\cos 2w\right),

a figure eight in space that crosses itself at w=0w = 0 and w=πw = \pi, with kj=1k_j = 1, kc=300k_c = 300 and the robots spread over half the period. With ∥f′∥\|f'\| up to 36.7 and kc=300k_c = 300 the field is stiff, and the run uses ticks of 0.25 ms. After 50 s the largest path error is 7.7e-02 and the largest coordination error 1.4e-02, and the closest two robots are 0.82 apart.

10.3 Fig. 4: an open Lissajous curve that fills a cube

The second simulation: three robots on xj=cos⁡(njw)+mjx_j = \cos(n_j w) + m_j with n=(2,4.1,7.1)n = (\sqrt2, 4.1, 7.1) and m=(0.1,0.7,0)m = (0.1, 0.7, 0), kj=kc=1k_j = k_c = 1, for 100 s. Since 2\sqrt2 is irrational the curve never closes, and it fills the cube [−1,1]3+m[-1, 1]^3 + m. After 20 s the largest path error is 2.6e-03 (the paper: “almost zero after 20 seconds”). To measure the coverage the page cuts the cube into 10310^3 cells: in 100 s the three robots visit 95.0 % of them, and robot 1 alone 92.4 % [numerical].

10.4 Fig. 5: 21 robots on three paths (the example)

This is the run of the figures above, for 40 s. After 40 s the largest path error is 5.3e-03 and the largest coordination error 1.1e-04. Over the last 10 s the closest two robots are 0.60 apart: as the paper says, the robots never overlap, because robots with different ww could only meet where the paths cross ((±10,0)(\pm 10, 0) for the large circle and the ellipse, (0,±5)(0, \pm 5) for the ellipse and the small circle) at the same ww.

10.5 Fig. 6: a pattern on a torus

The fourth simulation: robots on the torus

f=((2+cosw1)cosw2,(2+cosw1)sinw2,sinw1), f = \left((2 + \cos w_1)\cos w_2,\ \ (2+\cos w_1)\sin w_2,\ \ \sin w_1\right),

with ẇ*=(−1,−1)\dot w^* = (-1, -1), so v=(0,0,0,−1,1)v = (0, 0, 0, -1, 1), kj=1k_j = 1 and kc=10k_c = 10. The paper picks 67 reference points by hand that spell “ICRA”; those points are not in the paper, so the page draws its own pattern, the letters “GVF”, with 28 points on a cycle graph that follows the strokes (drawn three times narrower in w2w_2, since the torus is three times wider around its axis than around its tube). After 20 s the largest surface error is 7.4e-03 and the largest coordination error 6.0e-03. Since all robots run at the same ẇ*\dot w^*, the pattern keeps its shape in the parameters and travels around the torus, around the tube and around the axis at once.

10.6 The two flights, in simulation

The flights use the scaled field that the paper states for them, ϕj=L(xj−fj(βw))\phi_j = L\,(x_j - f_j(\beta w)) with L=0.1L = 0.1 (and β=0.01\beta = 0.01 on the Lissajous curve, β1=0.005\beta_1 = 0.005 and β2=0.01\beta_2 = 0.01 on the torus). Up to a positive factor, which the partial normalisation removes, this is the field (3) for the path f(βw)f(\beta w) with the gains k/Lk/L and kcβ/L3k_c\,\beta/L^3 (one line of algebra, ours), and that is how the page flies it, with an airspeed of 12 m/s and a turn-rate limit of 0.8 rad/s (neither is in the paper). The simulated aircraft converge in a few minutes and then fly about one metre apart, the GPS bias, with path errors below 0.9 m on the Lissajous curve. The real flights also had wind (10 km/h) and an autopilot whose airspeed changes when it climbs; the paper reports errors of one to two metres. The page does not model the autopilot.

11 What changes with more robots, and what this page does not cover

More robots. Nothing in the field depends on NN: each robot computes its own χ[i]\chi^{[i]} from its own path and its neighbours’ ww, and the communication per robot depends on its number of neighbours only (two on a cycle, whatever NN). Theorem 1 holds for any NN [proved]. What changes is the speed: the slowest mode of the coordination has the graph’s λ2\lambda_2, which on a cycle falls as 4π2/N24\pi^2/N^2, and Section 4.4 divides it further by ∥f′∥2\|f'\|^2 [numerical], for the circle’s linearisation.

Not covered here.

  • Time-varying Δ[i,j](t)\Delta^{[i,j]}(t) and time-varying paths: the paper leaves them to future work.
  • Switching graphs: the paper’s conclusion points to consensus results for them; the page does not simulate them.
  • The safety certificate’s deadlocks (the paper’s remark, Wang et al. Section VII): the page shows robots that dodge, not robots that block each other.
  • The aircraft’s low-level loops (bank and climb), and the wind in the flights. The figure of Section 7 has a wind slider, which the program does not know about [numerical].
  • A coordination in Euclidean distance rather than in the parameter: the paper names it as future work.

12 Glossary

f[i]f^{[i]}
robot ii’s path f[i](w)f^{[i]}(w) or surface f[i](w1,w2)f^{[i]}(w_1, w_2), in ℝn\mathbb R^n.
w[i]w^{[i]}, ξ[i]\xi^{[i]}
robot ii’s virtual coordinate(s), and its generalised coordinate (x[i],w[i])(x^{[i]}, w^{[i]}).
ϕj[i]\phi^{[i]}_j, Φ\Phi
the path (or surface) errors xj−fj(w)x_j - f_j(w), and all of them stacked.
χ[i]\chi^{[i]}
robot ii’s coordinating guiding vector field, (5) or (17).
c[i]c^{[i]}, kck_c
the coordination function (7), and its gain.
Δ[i,j]\Delta^{[i,j]}, w*w^*
the desired parametric difference on the edge (i,j)(i, j), and a reference with Δ[i,j]=w[i]*−w[j]*\Delta^{[i,j]} = w^{[i]*} - w^{[j]*}.
LL, DD, λ2\lambda_2
the Laplacian and an incidence matrix of the graph, L=DD⊤L = DD^\top, and its smallest nonzero eigenvalue.
VV
the Lyapunov function of the proofs, (41) and (55).
vv, ẇ*\dot w^*
the extra vector of the surface field (14), and the desired parametric speeds of Theorem 2.
RR, α\alpha, 𝒟i\mathcal D_i
the safety distance, the gain of the barrier, and the robots robot ii keeps away from in (QP2).
vv (aircraft), θ\theta, σ\sigma
the airspeed, the course, and the angle from the field’s horizontal direction to the course.
θ̇d\dot\theta_d, kθk_\theta, aa, bb
the turn rate of the field’s direction (32), the heading gain, and the saturation limits of (31).
